# `ecommerce_daily_aov_within_bounds`

> A daily average order value above 5,000 has never been a real business day — it signals a pricing/quantity bug or bulk fraud, even if every row looks valid.

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain | [ecommerce](README.md) |
| Layer | **gold** — evaluated by the `gold` gate |
| Model | `gld_ecommerce__daily_kpis` (`ecommerce_gold_staging.gld_ecommerce__daily_kpis`) |
| Column | `average_order_value` |
| Check | `value_between` |
| Severity | `error` — a violation **stops the pipeline** |
| Defined in | [dbt/models/ecommerce/gold/_gold.yml](../../../dbt/models/ecommerce/gold/_gold.yml) |

## What it checks

`average_order_value` is between 1 and 5000 (inclusive).

## When it fails

The `gold` task of `medallion_ecommerce` fails, `publish_gold` doesn't run, and the batch is never added to `ecommerce_gold`: consumers keep the batches published before. `quality_report` marks the run as blocked and sends the alert, if one is configured.

The rows that broke the rule in its latest evaluation are kept in `dq_audit.ecommerce_daily_aov_within_bounds`.

## Tested by

Scenario **`bulk_order_anomaly`**: every line has quantity 900: each row is valid, the day is not.

```bash
make generate DOMAIN=ecommerce SCENARIO=bulk_order_anomaly BATCH=2026-10-20_bulk_order_anomaly
make pipeline DOMAIN=ecommerce BATCH=2026-10-20_bulk_order_anomaly
```

## Investigate

```sql
-- rows that broke the rule last time it ran
select * from dq_audit.ecommerce_daily_aov_within_bounds;

-- history of the rule
select batch_id, status, failures, recorded_at
from dq_audit.rule_results
where rule = 'ecommerce_daily_aov_within_bounds'
order by recorded_at desc;
```

## Definition

```yaml
value_between:
  min_value: 1
  max_value: 5000
```
